source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Review the testing procedure conducted and ensure all steps were correctly followed.
3. Identify which particular brake tests failed and why.
4. Make a detailed note of the conditions under which the test was performed (e.g., wet/dry roads, weather, brake condition before the test).
5. Document any abnormal noises, vibrations, or observances noted during the brake test.
6. Record the foot pressure used for the brake test, if applicable.
7. Include all quantitative data collected, such as brake application time, deceleration rate, stopping distances, and the amount of pedal travel.
8. Note the test results in comparison to the acceptable standard (e.g., brake efficiency percentage).
9. Take photographs if possible to visually document the failure.
10. Include a brief description of what the vehicle was doing at the time of failure (e.g., pulling to one side, excessive vibration).
